women_problem_title: They run real businesses, but remain invisible to the formal financial system
women_problem_text: Alternative credit scoring models currently used in East Africa rely heavily on mobile money transaction data — leaving out women whose businesses run on cash, and who depend on the trust of their savings group (chama/VICOBA) rather than digital data.
women_model_text: A focused 3-month core program gets each woman through financial literacy and the fastest formalization steps — followed by an open-ended continuation where she keeps building her record at her own pace, with loan-readiness assessed whenever her data genuinely supports it, not on a fixed deadline.

phase1_steps.title: Month 1: Selection & Baseline
phase1_steps.text: Entering through existing group leaders, selecting participants deliberately, and completing a baseline financial and readiness assessment.

phase1_steps.title: Month 2: Financial Literacy & Fast-Track Formalization
phase1_steps.text: Daily bookkeeping training begins alongside hands-on support starting NIDA and BRELA registration — the two steps most other formalization depends on.

phase1_steps.title: Month 3: TIN & Graduation to Self-Paced Continuation
phase1_steps.text: TIN registration completed. Each woman graduates into Phase 2 with a personal plan for her remaining formalization steps.

phase2_steps.title: Ongoing: Remaining Formalization
phase2_steps.text: Business license and bank account completed at each woman's own pace, with periodic light-touch check-ins rather than intensive coaching.

phase2_steps.title: Ongoing: Sustained Bookkeeping
phase2_steps.text: Continued daily use of Biashara Yangu builds a real, multi-month transaction and loan-repayment history — the actual evidence a lender needs.

phase2_steps.title: Whenever Ready: Loan Readiness & MFI Matching
phase2_steps.text: Once her data genuinely supports it — not on a fixed timeline — she's connected to a partner financial institution.

pilot_text: Biashara Yangu is a digital tool being piloted with our first cohort — one part of a broader BDS service, not the project itself.
policy_items: Tanzania's National Financial Inclusion Framework (2023–2028) has shifted from "access" toward "quality of usage."

Agricultural credit guarantee schemes are helping smallholder farmers access loans — but participating financial institutions still need to identify which farmer is trustworthy. That's where we fit in.
From July 2026, digital payments are legally required for crop sales through AMCOS — directly relevant to our agricultural participants.
women_status_note: We are at an early stage. Real participant numbers will be shown here once available.
youth_problem_text: Computers and internet access in schools are a good start, but without digital safety training, young people are at risk of online scams, harassment, and misuse of their personal information.
youth_status_note: This program is being redesigned from its original "Digital School Club" model — toward direct safety and advancement training, not just device access. Goal: connecting 100+ schools across Tanzania by 2030.
market_problem_title: Financial institutions struggle to reach — and understand — the unreached
market_problem_text: Rural, informal-sector women are frequently identified as a target market, but rarely understood well enough to actually design services for. Financial institutions often lack the ground-level research and trusted community access needed to find out why a given service isn't being adopted, and what would actually change that — research that's expensive and slow to build from scratch.
market_model_text: We conduct direct research into why unreached rural populations don't use specific financial products, and what would need to change for adoption — using a pool of trained graduate researchers who work directly in the communities we already have trust and reach in.
market_benefits: For financial institutions: real go-to-market research on the unreached rural segment specifically, plus a trusted community channel — reducing the cost of acquiring customers who are otherwise expensive and slow to reach.
For our graduate researchers: paid, meaningful employment conducting real fieldwork, building research and market-entry experience.
For rural communities: financial products and services actually designed around why they currently don't use them, not assumptions about them.
market_status_note: This program is in early design. We're seeking financial institution partners interested in shaping a pilot research engagement together.
